Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (name certification); Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office (register of companies); Notaría / Colegio Notarial de España (notarial deed execution); Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) for NIF registration.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), Articles 1-58 (SRL formation, capital, by-laws); Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil); Law 14/2013, de 27 de septiembre, de apoyo a los emprendedores, Articles 15-16 (expedited DUE telematic incorporation); Law 14/2014, de 24 de julio, de Navegación Marítima, Articles 145-150 (naviera / ship-fleet operator rules).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation), inscribed in the Registro Mercantil Provincial and processed through the Documento Único Electrónico (DUE) single point of filing.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 13 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada: minimum subscribed capital EUR 3,000, fully paid up at incorporation; capital represented by participaciones (EUR 1.00 nominal each or as by-laws provide); funds must be deposited in a Spanish bank account and evidenced by a bank capital-in-payment certificate (certificado de desembolso) delivered to the notary; non-cash contributions require an independent valuation report; no separate statutory escrow lock-box is required beyond the bank deposit certificate, but the deposit must remain in the corporate account until registry inscription.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety: each vessel under charter must hold a valid SOLAS Safety Equipment Certificate, a Safety Construction Certificate (hull, machinery, and electrical surveys), and a radio and navigation safety certificate; structural and load line surveys per the International Load Line Convention are required before flag registration, with periodic class inspections by an IACS-classification society (e.g., Lloyd's, DNV, BV). Onshore: the Spanish registered office must pass municipal fire-safety inspection and occupy a building with a first-occupancy license (licencia de primera ocupación) covering commercial use; workplace health-and-safety clearance is required under Law 31/1995 PRL for administrative employees; additionally, the company must adopt an ISPS Code-compliant security plan if operating in SOLAS-regulated ports, and an occupational medicine service contract must be in force for any crew or shore employees.

Paid-in capital rule: Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada: minimum subscribed capital EUR 3,000, fully paid up at incorporation; capital represented by participaciones (EUR 1.00 nominal each or as by-laws provide); funds must be deposited in a Spanish bank account and evidenced by a bank capital-in-payment certificate (certificado de desembolso) delivered to the notary; non-cash contributions require an independent valuation report; no separate statutory escrow lock-box is required beyond the bank deposit certificate, but the deposit must remain in the corporate account until registry inscription.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION: The founding shareholder, assembled in extraordinary general meeting, RESOLVED: (1) the subscription of 3,000 participaciones, each of EUR 1.00 nominal, totalling EUR 3,000 fully paid-up capital, is ratified; (2) the registered office is established at the address appearing in the by-laws, within the territorial jurisdiction of the Mercantile Registry of [Province]; (3) [Name] is appointed as Sole Administrator (Administrador Único) with the full powers enumerated in the by-laws, including representation before courts, tax authorities, banks, notaries, and the maritime administration; (4) the Sole Administrator is authorized to execute the DUE filing, obtain the NIF, open bank accounts, and procure all operational licenses; (5) all prior acts of the founders are expressly ratified.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

Dirección General de la Marina Mercante (General Directorate of the Merchant Marine), Ministerio de Transportes y Movilidad Sostenible, in coordination with the Capitanía Marítima of the vessel registration port and the Registro Especial de Buques y Empresas Navieras.

Category: Licencia de Empresa Naviera / Autorización de Armador y Registro en el Registro Especial de Empresas Navieras, together with flag-state vessel registration (abanderamiento) in the Registro de Buques y Empresas Navieras; each chartered vessel must carry an ISM Code Safety Management Certificate and a Documento de Cumplimiento de Gestión de la Seguridad (company DOC).

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; operative registration forms: modelo 036 (self-registration in the Census de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores), modelo 037 (simplified variant for SMEs), and the notarial/registry procedure for corporate incorporation.

E-government filing portal

Foreign persons forming a Spanish SL: (1) obtain a provisional NIF for the société from AEAT (via modelo 036) at the time the public deed of incorporation is executed before a Spanish Notary Public; (2) record the deed in the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central / Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office); (3) after registry inscription, return to AEAT with the registry certificate to receive the definitive Spanish NIF (letter plus 8 digits) with updated modelo 036; (4) non-resident shareholders/directors must separately apply for their NIF-ES (modelo 030 or 036) and appoint a tax representative resident in Spain where AEAT requirements or the regime of the Non-Resident Income Tax so demand; (5) the SL must file an annual annual accounts deposit and interactive Census declaration (modelo 036/037 modifications) whenever capital, activity, or management data change. For the impugnante the SL is also obliged to register in the IVA Census before commencing the leasing activity.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation (the SL is a resident corporate taxpayer under Ley 27/2014 del Impuesto sobre Sociedades; Spanish-situs worldwide income is taxed at a 25% headline CIT rate; shareholders are separately taxed in personal/ corporate income tax on distributions, and no partnership flow-through is available for an SL). — Foreign persons forming a Spanish SL: (1) obtain a provisional NIF for the société from AEAT (via modelo 036) at the time the public deed of incorporation is executed before a Spanish Notary Public; (2) record the deed in the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central / Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office); (3) after registry inscription, return to AEAT with the registry certificate to receive the definitive Spanish NIF (letter plus 8 digits) with updated modelo 036; (4) non-resident shareholders/directors must separately apply for their NIF-ES (modelo 030 or 036) and appoint a tax representative resident in Spain where AEAT requirements or the regime of the Non-Resident Income Tax so demand; (5) the SL must file an annual annual accounts deposit and interactive Census declaration (modelo 036/037 modifications) whenever capital, activity, or management data change. For the impugnante the SL is also obliged to register in the IVA Census before commencing the leasing activity.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation (the SL is a resident corporate taxpayer under Ley 27/2014 del Impuesto sobre Sociedades; Spanish-situs worldwide income is taxed at a 25% headline CIT rate; shareholders are separately taxed in personal/ corporate income tax on distributions, and no partnership flow-through is available for an SL).

Available election forms

No check-the-box flow-through election exists in Spanish corporate law. Statutory alternatives relevant to the vessel-leasing group: (a) optional tax consolidation (Régimen de Consolidación Fiscal, articles 55-70 LIS) available to resident groups holding at least 75% interests and filing consolidated tax returns; (b) special tonnage-tax regime for eligible ocean-going ships (article 113 LIS, applicable to vessels registered in the Spanish or Canary Islands special registry under EU State-aid clearance), which the entity may elect for qualifying offshore support vessels; (c) the cash-basis VAT scheme (régimen de criterio de caja) available below EUR 2,000,000 turnover; (d) mandatory application of EU ATAD anti-hybrid rules (articles 78-81 LIS) that automatically re-characterize or disallow payments in dual-resident and hybrid instrument/structure mismatches; (e) the option to petition binding advance pricing agreements and tax-rulings through AEAT for maritime-charter margins.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general turnover exemption threshold exists for VAT registration: any taxable person habitually carrying out business or professional activity in Spanish territory must apply for a NIF and register in the IVA Census (modelo 036) before commencing operations. Simplified and special regimes apply only for certain SME categories (e.g., simplified regime below EUR 250,000 annual turnover in eligible sectors), and the cash-based accounting is restricted to businesses below EUR 2,000,000 of annual turnover. Non-established suppliers of B2B services uploaded through the reverse-charge mechanism (for which the Spanish customer is the taxable person) also require a NIF-ES and, where applicable, the registration for an agent/representative. For this offshore vessel charter, the Spanish SL chartering to non-residents generally triggers no positive Spanish output VAT under place-of-supply rules, while charters to Spanish-established customers require full IVA registration without threshold relief.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Zero-rating with credit (0% VAT) is available under article 21 LIVA for exports of goods dispatched to third countries (including vessels and spare parts) where the goods leave EU customs territory within 90 days after delivery (or within the longer documented transport period, max. 180 days when the carrier itinerary justifies extension). Services directly relating to international maritime transport, including the chartering (time, voyage or demise) and auxiliary offshore support-vessel services, qualify as zero-rated where (i) the customer is established outside Spain/EU (article 69 LIVA), or (ii) the Spanish-established customer cannot demonstrate that the effective utilisation and exploitation takes place outside the EU; conversely, where the vessel's operational and trading area lies entirely on the high seas in third-country offshore fields, the 'effective use and enjoyment' rule of article 70.Dos.5º LIVA moves the place of supply outside the EU, thereby excluding the supply from Spanish VAT entirely. The fulfilment of EU export conditions, including customs supervision by the Spanish Customs Office for the DUA and subsequent departure control results (ATLAS), is subject to documentary proof by the exporter before any refund is properly accepted.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo / AES electronic declaration) accepted by Customs with definitive export status ('Estadística', salida efectiva) from Spanish territory
  • Consultation of the goods release/leaving record via AEAT's ATLAS departure website, evidencing physical exit from EU territory
  • Bill of Lading (B/L) or sea waybill accompanied by the vessel's delivery/redelivery certificate (signage of the port authority at the port of destination outside the EU)
  • Inward Remittance Certificate (certificado de banco español acreditativo del cobro de la exportación) demonstrating the collection and shown application of the invoice within the legal collection term, together with SWIFT MT103 transfer confirmations
  • Charter-party contract, freight invoice and the IMO-vessel maritime despacho/expedition dossier (notificación de despacho portuario) documenting the offshore voyage and platform service locations
  • Commercial invoice, insurance certificate (certificado de seguro marítimo), and, where applicable, the non-VAT certificate of the non-resident charterer's establishment in a third country

Large enterprises (annual turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000) and VAT groups must file near-real-time invoicing records with AEAT via the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) system using authenticated SOAP/XML-API calls (services SII-IS, SII-FI, SII-IV y SII-CM), with each invoice submitted within 4 days from issue/entry; all taxpayers must use certified billing software meeting the anti-fraud specifications of Real Decreto 1007/2023 (Verifact-requirements: incorruptible hash, QR code and electronic delivery of invoice files); in Basque territories (Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa, Araba) the TicketBAI digital stamping system further obliges real-time technical clearance before issuing each invoice, while in Navarra the regional equivalent applies; non-resident operators are equally bound when issuing Spanish invoices.

AEAT actively audits offshore-vessel charters under export-compliance procedures (verificaciones del domicilio fiscal, customs exit checks and CIVI-VAC international exchange of information). Any unjustified zero-rating or export exemption triggers retroactive VAT assessment for the affected tax periods, together with full late-payment interest (interés de demora). Quantitative sanctions under Ley 58/2003 General Tributaria: minor infractions 50%; serious infractions 50-100%; aggravated serious infractions for means or amount 75-150%; very serious infractions 100-150%. Fraudulent concealment to reduce VAT beyond EUR 120,000 constitutes a criminal tax offence (Código Penal article 305 and 305 bis) punishable with imprisonment of 1 to 6 years per period, accessory penalties of loss of subsidies and binding electoral or banking records, disbarment from certain maritime registries, publication of sanctions, and monetary fines up to six times the defrauded amount. The burden of proving the high-seas place of supply and the effective third-country exploitation lies on the taxpayer; absence or falsification of any element in the documentation bundle (customs DUA, B/L, remittance certificate) causes clawback for the entire open period, which for essential-tax data can be extended to four years.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain is a full-currency-convertibility jurisdiction within the Eurozone. The euro is freely convertible and the capital account is fully liberalised under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. No prior Central Bank permit is required for current-account or capital-account payments to or from non-residents. Cross-border profit remittance from a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is not exchange-controlled and is generally permitted after lawful corporate distribution; however, the Spanish paying company must operate the applicable non-resident income tax withholding, generally at the statutory rate of 19% where no tax treaty reduction applies, and must retain the certified board resolution, audited financial statements and the shareholder tax-residence certificate for the remitting bank. For balance-of-payments statistics, the bank may be obliged to file a declarative report to Banco de España under the Spanish external-transactions framework; this is a transparency requirement and does not constitute an authorisation or a conversion restriction.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. An offshore supply-vessel lessor can invoice in EUR, USD or any freely accepted currency, and the resulting proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency bank accounts or converted without Banco de España approval. There is no statutory timeline for converting export or service revenue into EUR. The treasury obligation is documentary: export/offshore charter revenue must be supported by approved invoices, the underlying charter party, proof of services or delivery and bank source-of-funds documentation if requested under Spanish Law 10/2010. Where proceeds are routed through Spanish banks, the transaction may be reported for balance-of-payments statistical purposes if the relevant threshold is met; this is a filing, not a convertibility check.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España, the national central bank of Spain, acting within the Eurosystem and the Single Supervisory Mechanism; the Ministry of Economy, Commerce and Business retains the residual responsibility for external-transaction statistical declarations and foreign-investment filings

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium-low for the offshore marine charter model. EU/EEA authorised e-money institutions may passport payment services into Spain, but they cannot take deposits, hold principal balances as custodians or provide full maritime escrow services in the manner of a licensed credit institution. UK-based EMI firms do not benefit from EU passporting after Brexit and would require a Spanish payment-agent arrangement or local licensing. Such digital platforms can be accepted only as ancillary clearing providers for FX conversion, petty expense cards or payment aggregation, while the core capital, escrow and charter-hire account should sit in a Spanish first-tier bank to satisfy Law 10/2010 supervisory expectations.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Offshore vessel flag or bareboat re-charter chain leading to high-risk jurisdiction hits or an opaque beneficial-ownership chain including Panama, the Marshall Islands, the Cayman Islands or Malta.

Root cause: Offshore vessel flag or bareboat re-charter chain leading to high-risk jurisdiction hits or an opaque beneficial-ownership chain including Panama, the Marshall Islands, the Cayman Islands or Malta.

Defense evidence: Full ownership chain chart from the Spanish S.L. to each natural-person UBO; certified maritime registry certificates for flag and vessel registration; valid ISM Safety Management Certificate and ISPS security compliance certificates; crewing and manning agreements; International Tonnage Certificate; AML/KYC explanation of each intermediary; sanctions screening reports from EU, UK and OFAC lists; and an independent corporate registry verification confirming registered and beneficial ownership.
Incoming charter-hire or disbursements from Latin American or African state-related oil and gas entities, with routing via correspondent banks located in higher-risk corridors.

Root cause: Incoming charter-hire or disbursements from Latin American or African state-related oil and gas entities, with routing via correspondent banks located in higher-risk corridors.

Defense evidence: Signed offshore support-vessel charter party; original or certified invoice ledger; vessel Automatic Identification System (AIS) tracking for the applicable hire period; Brazil, Mexico, Colombia or Ecuador tax-domicile certificates where counterparties reside; board resolutions approving the transaction; trade-compliance declarations certifying no UN/EU/OFAC sanctioned counterparties or cargoes; and verified complete registry documentation for the vessel.
Missing documentation of the initial capital injection or foreign-currency source, causing refusal to open a capital-escrow account or classification of the S.L. as a high-risk PEP-related entity.

Root cause: Missing documentation of the initial capital injection or foreign-currency source, causing refusal to open a capital-escrow account or classification of the S.L. as a high-risk PEP-related entity.

Defense evidence: Statutory share-subscription agreement and Spanish notarial deed of incorporation; six-month account statements from the parent or ultimate funding entity; tax-residence certificate for each UBO; register of beneficial owners extract; NIE certificates for signatories; public deed of capital increase where contributions are subsequent; and a signed covenant letter stating that the funds will be credited to the Spanish capital account and disclosed to Banco de España for balance-of-payments statistics if required.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Inbound equity contributions must be routed through a Spanish bank using a clearly demarcated rail. For incoming payments from EU jurisdictions, a SEPA Credit Transfer to the Spanish S.L. IBAN is acceptable; for non-EEA injections, SWIFT MT103 remains the mandatory wire protocol. The remittance instruction should expressly refer to the public deed and purpose such as 'capital contribution to ES_SL' to prevent reclassification as a shareholder loan. The bank will apply Law 10/2010 source-of-funds checks and, where applicable, process the Banco de España balance-of-payments statistical declaration. Capital funds should land in a dedicated capital-escrow or corporate operating account, and the resolutions, notarised deeds, payment instructions and proof of source must be maintained in the treasury onboarding file.Outbound charter-hire, bunker, crew and supply payments are cleared by SEPA Credit Transfer within the EEA and by SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA counterparties. For documentary trade settlement, Spanish banks provide commercial letter-of-credit facilities under SWIFT MT700 and standby letters of credit under SWIFT MT760 for off-hire, mobilisation or performance guarantees. Escrow-maritime disbursements are acceptable where a Spanish notary or a regulated financial institution acts as escrow agent, releasing funds only upon presentation of the charter-party delivery certificate, inspection report or signed pay-off authorisation. Every outbound instruction must carry a matching vendor identity and apposite purpose narrative to maintain the Spanish VAT, corporate-tax and AML audit trail.Deliverable EUR/USD forward exchange contracts entered for bona fide treasury hedging of foreign-currency charter-hire and opex exposure.Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps matching the long-term currency profile of vessel-leasing receivables with USD or EUR liabilities.Non-deliverable forwards on illiquid or restricted currencies, including MXN, COP and BRL, when the offshore charter model generates structurally mismatched currency receipts; such NDFs are permitted in Spain with ISDA documentation and settlement margin in EUR.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium-low for the offshore marine charter model. EU/EEA authorised e-money institutions may passport payment services into Spain, but they cannot take deposits, hold principal balances as custodians or provide full maritime escrow services in the manner of a licensed credit institution. UK-based EMI firms do not benefit from EU passporting after Brexit and would require a Spanish payment-agent arrangement or local licensing. Such digital platforms can be accepted only as ancillary clearing providers for FX conversion, petty expense cards or payment aggregation, while the core capital, escrow and charter-hire account should sit in a Spanish first-tier bank to satisfy Law 10/2010 supervisory expectations.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% general Spanish Corporate Income Tax rate. Newly incorporated entities generally qualify for a 15% rate during the first profitable tax period and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory conditions and exclusions.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends and other profit distributions to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions, treaty relief, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive implementation, and anti-abuse rules. Qualifying EU or EEA corporate shareholders may obtain exemption where minimum ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form, and anti-abuse conditions are met.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Modelo 200 is generally due within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the normal filing window is 1 to 25 July of the following year. Modelo 202 is generally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December; electronic filing is normally available until the 20th calendar day, with the applicable banking-day rule for direct debit. The return must be filed even where no tax is payable if a filing obligation exists.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Generally filed during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December, based on the applicable statutory calculation method. Large companies may be required to use the minimum-payment method based on accounting profit and relevant exclusions.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Generally EUR 250,000 per related counterparty and transaction type, aggregated under the applicable Spanish rules, is the principal threshold relevant to the exemption from full related-party documentation. Local File and Master File requirements are subject to additional exemptions, transaction categories, group-size rules, and content requirements. Country-by-Country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million in the preceding fiscal year. Modelo 232 may be required for specified related-party transaction thresholds and tax-haven transactions.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a single stand-alone Cayman-style Economic Substance Regulation for all companies. Substance is enforced through the General Tax Law anti-abuse rule, conflict-in-the-application provisions, simulation doctrine, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled foreign company rules, EU anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation, treaty principal-purpose tests, and transfer-pricing requirements. A Spanish SL should maintain real decision-making, appropriately qualified personnel, premises or operational capacity, vessel-management and chartering records, commercial risk control, bank and accounting autonomy, and evidence that services and assets are actually used. A conduit company receiving dividends, interest, royalties, or charter income without commercial substance may lose treaty or domestic exemption benefits and may face reassessment, interest, penalties, and withholding liability.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Corporate Income Tax evasion and fraudulent accounting

Statutory sanction: Administrative tax penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, plus tax, interest, and potential loss of tax benefits. Where the tax defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 in a tax year, the conduct may constitute a criminal tax offence punishable generally by imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of up to six times the amount defrauded. Aggravated cases may carry imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and substantially higher fines.

Director personal liability: Directors and de facto managers may incur civil liability for unpaid taxes and penalties where statutory derivation requirements are met, criminal liability for intentional participation, and liability for accounting or document offences. Courts may impose professional disqualification and asset measures. Travel restrictions or passport measures may be ordered in criminal proceedings where legally justified; imprisonment is not automatic and requires judicial proceedings and conviction.
Transfer-pricing manipulation

Statutory sanction: The Spanish Tax Agency may make a primary adjustment, impose secondary adjustment consequences, assess withholding or indirect tax, and apply documentation or valuation penalties. Failure to provide required documentation or provision of materially incomplete or inaccurate documentation may generate specific penalties, generally calculated by reference to the affected transaction or tax data, subject to statutory caps.

Director personal liability: Directors may face administrative derivation liability where they caused or tolerated non-compliance, and criminal exposure where the conduct forms part of intentional tax fraud. Mere use of a low-margin model is not unlawful if supported by functions, assets, risks, comparables, and reliable records.
Undeclared permanent establishment or false operational location

Statutory sanction: Spain may attribute profits to a Spanish permanent establishment or Spanish resident company, assess Corporate Income Tax, VAT, withholding, payroll taxes, interest, and penalties, and challenge treaty claims under domestic anti-abuse rules.

Director personal liability: Directors may be personally liable for derived tax debts and may face criminal tax exposure where concealment is intentional and the statutory criminal thresholds are met.
Improper treaty, EU exemption, or beneficial-ownership claim

Statutory sanction: Spain may deny treaty or EU relief, assess withholding at the domestic rate, charge interest, and impose withholding and information-return penalties. Anti-abuse rules may also deny participation exemption or interest and royalty exemption.

Director personal liability: Directors who knowingly approve false residence certificates, sham arrangements, or misleading withholding files may face civil, administrative, and criminal consequences depending on intent and tax loss.
Value Added Tax and customs fraud

Statutory sanction: VAT reassessment, repayment of improperly claimed refunds, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties may apply. Serious or fraudulent VAT conduct may trigger criminal tax proceedings where statutory thresholds are met.

Director personal liability: Directors and responsible officers may face derived tax liability and criminal exposure for deliberate false invoices, fabricated transport evidence, or coordinated VAT fraud.
Anti-money laundering and terrorist-financing violations

Statutory sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, very serious breaches may attract substantial administrative fines, potentially reaching the higher statutory amounts for entities and responsible officers, together with public reprimand, temporary prohibition from holding management positions, or withdrawal of authorization where applicable. Serious and minor breaches carry lower but material fines and compliance measures.

Director personal liability: Directors, compliance officers, and officers responsible for the breach may be fined personally and may face management disqualification. Deliberate money laundering may constitute a criminal offence with imprisonment and asset confiscation. Travel restrictions may be imposed by a court in criminal proceedings where legally justified.
Sanctions, export-control, and maritime compliance

Statutory sanction: Administrative fines, transaction invalidation, asset blocking, license suspension or revocation, seizure, and criminal sanctions may apply under the relevant sanctions, customs, maritime, and criminal laws. Contractual and insurance coverage may also be void or unenforceable.

Director personal liability: Directors and managers may face personal administrative and criminal liability for knowing or reckless participation. Asset freezing, judicial travel restrictions, disqualification, and imprisonment may be ordered where the applicable offence and procedural requirements are satisfied.
Illegal distributions and creditor prejudice

Statutory sanction: Improper distributions may require restitution with interest, director compensation for losses, corporate-law sanctions, insolvency clawback, and tax recharacterization as dividends or hidden distributions. The transaction may also generate withholding tax and penalties.

Director personal liability: Directors may be jointly or personally liable for unlawful distributions, delayed insolvency filings, creditor damage, and tax debts under the applicable statutory conditions. Criminal insolvency liability may apply to fraudulent asset depletion or concealment.
False invoicing, document destruction, or obstruction of tax audit

Statutory sanction: Separate accounting, information, obstruction, and tax penalties may apply. Serious conduct may constitute document falsification, obstruction of justice, or tax fraud, with fines, professional restrictions, imprisonment, and tax reassessment.

Director personal liability: The individuals who ordered, approved, signed, or knowingly benefited from false records may be prosecuted personally. Corporate limited liability does not protect intentional personal criminal conduct.
